sections.h2: Where to record in Travis County
sections.html:
The Travis County Clerk's Recording Division files and keeps real property records, including deeds and tax liens. The main office is at 5501 Airport Blvd., Ste. 100B, Austin, TX 78751, open 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The mailing address is P.O. Box 149325, Austin, TX 78714, and the recording phone line is (512) 854-9188.

Two sub-stations are open 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM: the Civil Family Courthouse at 1700 Guadalupe St., 4th Floor, Ste. 4.300, Austin 78701, and the Raul Martinez Office Building at 4011 McKinney Falls Pkwy #1200, Austin 78744. The Guadalupe Street location takes Official Public Record recordings, DBA filings and marriage licenses with no appointment, but not plats.

Travis County includes Austin and is large and growing, with about 1,389,670 residents in 2025, up from 1,290,188 in 2020. The typical owner-occupied home is valued around $523,000, and median gross rent is $1,744. Deed work here includes many investor sales, estate transfers and rental properties, so a clean recorded chain of title is what keeps a closing on schedule.

Heavy volume keeps the recording desk busy. Deeds, releases of lien, trustee sale notices and plats all flow through the same division. Filing early in the day, or going through a title company's e-filing channel, avoids most delays at the counter.

Bring or mail the original signed document, since the clerk will not record a copy. You can file real property documents in person or by mail, and recording is complete as soon as the clerk receives the document.

Most documents other than plats are scanned, given an instrument number and returned the same day, by mail or on the spot for walk-in customers. Subdivision plats are not returned the same day. Pay by cash, credit card, check or money order payable to Travis County Clerk. A card payment adds $3 on transactions under $100, or 3 percent on $100 or more.

A deed must also meet the state execution rule: acknowledged before a notary or other officer, or sworn before two subscribing witnesses, under Property Code Section 12.001(b).

An Official Public Records document costs $25.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, part of a page or rider. Leave at least three inches of space at the bottom of the last page, or the extra page fee applies.

Selected Travis County Clerk recording fees

Discharges, DD214 filings, and child support liens and releases carry no charge.

The clerk's public records search is at tccsearch.org. Indexes for most recorded documents are online, and redacted images run from the mid 1980s to the present. A redacted image has personal identifiers such as Social Security numbers blocked.

Court case data updates every 24 hours, and images of newly filed documents take about 72 hours to appear. Older documents are held in the clerk's permanent library, which has millions of documents dating to the 1800s, with the oldest on microfilm.

  • Printed from online at home: free, marked as an unofficial copy.
  • Clerk-made or emailed copies: $1.00 per page.
  • Certified copies: $5.00 per document plus $1.00 per page.
  • Self-serve photocopies: 20 cents per page; microfilm or computer printouts: 25 cents.

A basic electronic search for one name or business is free, plus the cost of copies. Searching microfilm or paper data costs $10.00 per name for each ten-year period.

Grantor and grantee searches run $10.00 per name for up to ten years. Federal and state tax searches are $10.00 each, and UCC-11 searches are $15.00 per debtor. For a deeper search, ask the clerk for an estimate.

eRecording is limited to certain filers under Local Government Code Section 195.003. They include Texas attorneys, banks and credit unions, title insurance companies and agents, federally approved lenders, regulated lenders and state agencies.

The clerk keeps a list of approved submitter companies and welcomes anyone interested in becoming a submitter to call. A homeowner selling alone does not qualify directly, so most sellers go through a title company, which typically e-files the deed on closing day.

sections.h2: Liens, tax and the rest of the record
sections.html:
The record shows more than the deed. Liens, trustee sale notices and tax liens are filed with the same clerk. A trustee sale notice for real estate is posted for $2.00, and state and federal tax liens have their own filing charges.

Property tax runs through a separate system: the appraisal district sets value, local taxing units bill, and the clerk only records documents. For closing figures, ask the Travis County tax office for the current bill. Before listing, search the owner's name for open liens and make sure the deed in your chain matches the name on the contract.

A certified copy is made by a clerk, who stamps it as an accurate and complete reproduction of the original. Certification costs $5.00 per document plus $1.00 per page, and you can request one by phone, email or in person.

No recording sticker goes on the last page of a certified copy, so one extra $4.00 page is always added. Copies of federal documents cost $1.50 per page and state documents $1.00 per page. An 18 by 24 inch plat copy is $3.00 per page. If you need a certified copy of a vesting deed for a sale, ask early, because a lender or title company usually wants the recorded instrument number too.

Most fees cannot be refunded. A clerical error may qualify, but a service already performed generally is not refundable.

sections.h2: A short checklist before you sell
sections.html:
Before you list, pull your recorded deed and read it against the name on the contract. Search your own name for open liens, and check that any old mortgage has a recorded release. If the house came through an estate, ask the title company what probate papers it needs on file.

Bring the original signed and notarized deed if you file yourself. If a title company handles it, it will usually e-file on closing day and send you the recorded instrument number.

faqs.q: Where is the Travis County Clerk recording office?
faqs.a: The main office is at 5501 Airport Blvd., Ste. 100B, Austin, TX 78751. Sub-stations at 1700 Guadalupe St. and 4011 McKinney Falls Pkwy also take recordings, on 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM hours.

faqs.q: What is the Travis County fee for a deed?
faqs.a: Expect $25.00 on page one and $4.00 on every page after it, plus $0.25 for each indexed name beyond five. A missing grantee mailing address adds $20.00 or twice the recording fee.

faqs.q: Will the clerk record a photocopy of my deed?
faqs.a: No. The clerk requires the original with original signatures. Plan on filing a notarized original.

faqs.q: Can I search Travis County property records for free?
faqs.a: Yes, for online indexes and images. Printing at home is free and carries an unofficial copy mark. Searches of microfilm or paper records cost $10.00 per name per ten years.

faqs.q: How long do new documents take to show online?
faqs.a: Images of newly filed documents take about 72 hours to appear online. Recording itself is complete when the clerk receives the document.
